title: Refactor ghost-node reconciliation and compact provisioning paths
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Background: The autoscaler and capacity planner still carry two separate reconciliation paths that create transient 'ghost' nodes (nodes allocated in planner state but never fully provisioned) and duplicate provisioning side effects. This ticket consolidates the reconciliation flow, isolates provisioning sidecars, upgrades k8s client libraries, and removes a brittle custom cache layer that causes delayed eviction and memory pressure. Goals: 1) Eliminate ghost-node window by unifying allocation commit to a single canonical state transition. 2) Reduce median provisioning latency by 25% for ephemeral nodes. 3) Remove the legacy in-memory cache in favor of the snapshot+sequence store we maintain in planner snapshots. 4) Upgrade k8s client to v0.29 and go to 1.21 to resolve watch flaps. 5) Add e2e traces and metrics to observe lease lifecycle from allocation -> healthy -> eviction.
acceptance_criteria: No observed ghost-node allocations in synthetic run (50k simulated requests) over 4 hours
Provisioning path simplified to single code path with <10% duplicated code across controllers
End-to-end median provisioning latency reduced by >=25% in benchmark cluster
k8s client upgraded and integration tests pass in CI with live watch scenarios
New lease lifecycle spans emitted and visible in tracing dashboard with per-node timing
technical_notes: Modules to touch: pkg/autoscaler/reconcile.go, pkg/provisioner/allocator.go, pkg/lease/snapshot_store.go, cmd/node-sidecar/main.go
Remove legacy cache: replace pkg/capacity/cache with snapshot_store backed reads; migration job will run at startup to reconcile stale keys
Kubernetes client-go: bump from v0.27.x -> v0.29.2; update informer factories and Replace Deprecated APIs used in watch handlers
Go toolchain: target go1.21 for performance and improved GC; update CI matrix
Memory allocation target: reduce heap churn in reconcile loop by 30% (use object pools for ephemeral structs and avoid fmt.Sprintf allocations), run pprof before/after
Tracing: add OpenTelemetry spans around allocation commit and node-ready transition; emit attributes: node_id, allocator_version, sequence_id
Metrics: add histogram for provisioning_duration_seconds and counter for ghost_node_detected_total (should be 0 post-migration)
Risky areas: failure during snapshot migration can temporarily stall capacity planner — mitigation: migration feature-flagged with roll-forward/rollback paths
Compatibility: maintain legacy lease file format for 2 weeks after rollout; include a compatibility shim in snapshot_store
Estimate assumptions: 2 devs full time for 3 sprints; includes unit tests, integration tests, and 2-stage canary rollout
testing_plan: Unit tests for snapshot_store and allocator modules (cover edge states)
Integration harness: extend existing capacity-simulator to inject watch flaps and GC pressure
Canary run: 10% of fleet routed to new reconciler with doubled observability retention for 48h
Chaos test: simulate kube-apiserver restart and verify no ghost nodes on reconverge
Performance benchmark: run 3 x 1h runs on perf-cluster and compare median provisioning latency and allocation throughput
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged default-off merge to main behind autoscaler.v2 flag
Smoke canary: enable flag in staging and run smoke harness for 6h
Gradual canary: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with metrics thresholds gating each step
Fallback: toggle autoscaler.v2=false to revert to previous reconciler within 5 minutes; maintain legacy compatibility shim for 14 days
Postmortem window: monitor for 7 days after 100% rollout and capture observations into config-change playbook
